verdict.rationale: Solo 2 documents a physical touch on its capacitive sensor to confirm operations. It also supports passkeys/WebAuthn, PIV and OpenPGP, so touch-gated user presence is the product's own capability. Nothing in the evidence shows this touch being used, or documented for use, as an approval gate for automated or agent-initiated actions, so applying it there depends on outside integration. missing for 10: documented integration of touch-confirmation into agent or automation approval flows, guidance on enforcing touch for sensitive non-login actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require a physical key touch as the human-approval step for sensitive automated or agent-initiated actions

citations.quote: When prompted, touch the capacitive sensor on your Solo 2 to confirm.
It's a USB+NFC device that protects your accounts with passkeys/WebAuthn, and also speaks OATH (TOTP/HOTP), PIV, and OpenPGP.
